verses.en: As snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honour is not seemly for a fool.
verses.pt: Como a neve no verão, e como a chuva no tempo da ceifa, assim não convém ao tolo a honra.
verses.en_web: Like snow in summer, and as rain in harvest, so honor is not fitting for a fool.
verses.en_bbe: Like snow in summer and rain when the grain is being cut, so honour is not natural for the foolish.

verses.en: As the bird by wandering, as the swallow by flying, so the curse causeless shall not come.
verses.pt: Como o pássaro no seu vaguear, como a andorinha no seu voar, assim a maldição sem causa não encontra pouso.
verses.en_web: Like a fluttering sparrow, like a darting swallow, so the undeserved curse doesn’t come to rest.
verses.en_bbe: As the sparrow in her wandering and the swallow in her flight, so the curse does not come without a cause.

verses.en: A whip for the horse, a bridle for the ass, and a rod for the fool’s back.
verses.pt: O açoite é para o cavalo, o freio para o jumento, e a vara para as costas dos tolos.
verses.en_web: A whip is for the horse, a bridle for the donkey, and a rod for the back of fools!
verses.en_bbe: A whip for the horse, a mouth-bit for the ass, and a rod for the back of the foolish.

verses.en: Answer not a fool according to his folly, lest thou also be like unto him.
verses.pt: Não respondas ao tolo segundo a sua estultícia, para que também não te faças semelhante a ele.
verses.en_web: Don’t answer a fool according to his folly, lest you also be like him.
verses.en_bbe: Do not give to the foolish man a foolish answer, or you will be like him.

verses.en: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own conceit.
verses.pt: Responde ao tolo segundo a sua estultícia, para que ele não seja sábio aos seus próprios olhos.
verses.en_web: Answer a fool according to his folly, lest he be wise in his own eyes.
verses.en_bbe: Give a foolish man a foolish answer, or he will seem wise to himself.

verses.en: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool cutteth off the feet, and drinketh damage.
verses.pt: Os pés decepa, e o dano bebe, quem manda mensagens pela mão dum tolo.
verses.en_web: One who sends a message by the hand of a fool is cutting off feet and drinking violence.
verses.en_bbe: He who sends news by the hand of a foolish man is cutting off his feet and drinking in damage.

verses.en: The legs of the lame are not equal: so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
verses.pt: As pernas do coxo pendem frouxas; assim é o provérbio na boca dos tolos.
verses.en_web: Like the legs of the lame that hang loose, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
verses.en_bbe: The legs of one who has no power of walking are hanging loose; so is a wise saying in the mouth of the foolish.

verses.en: As he that bindeth a stone in a sling, so is he that giveth honour to a fool.
verses.pt: Como o que ata a pedra na funda, assim é aquele que dá honra ao tolo.
verses.en_web: As one who binds a stone in a sling, so is he who gives honor to a fool.
verses.en_bbe: Giving honour to a foolish man is like attempting to keep a stone fixed in a cord.

verses.en: As a thorn goeth up into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
verses.pt: Como o espinho que entra na mão do ébrio, assim é o provérbio na mão dos tolos.
verses.en_web: Like a thorn bush that goes into the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fools.
verses.en_bbe: Like a thorn which goes up into the hand of a man overcome by drink, so is a wise saying in the mouth of a foolish man.

verses.en: The great God that formed all things both rewardeth the fool, and rewardeth transgressors.
verses.pt: Como o flecheiro que fere a todos, assim é aquele que assalaria ao transeunte tolo, ou ao ébrio.
verses.en_web: As an archer who wounds all, so is he who hires a fool or he who hires those who pass by.
verses.en_bbe: Like an archer wounding all who go by, is a foolish man overcome by drink.

verses.en: As a dog returneth to his vomit, so a fool returneth to his folly.
verses.pt: Como o cão que torna ao seu vômito, assim é o tolo que reitera a sua estultícia.
verses.en_web: As a dog that returns to his vomit, so is a fool who repeats his folly.
verses.en_bbe: Like a dog going back to the food which he has not been able to keep down, is the foolish man doing his foolish acts over again.

verses.en: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? there is more hope of a fool than of him.
verses.pt: Vês um homem que é sábio a seus próprios olhos? Maior esperança há para o tolo do que para ele.
verses.en_web: Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
verses.en_bbe: Have you seen a man who seems to himself to be wise? There is more hope for the foolish than for him.

verses.en: The slothful man saith, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets.
verses.pt: Diz o preguiçoso: Um leão está no caminho; um leão está nas ruas.
verses.en_web: The sluggard says, “There is a lion in the road! A fierce lion roams the streets!”
verses.en_bbe: The hater of work says, There is a lion in the way; a lion is in the streets.

verses.en: As the door turneth upon his hinges, so doth the slothful upon his bed.
verses.pt: Como a porta se revolve nos seus gonzos, assim o faz o preguiçoso na sua cama.
verses.en_web: As the door turns on its hinges, so does the sluggard on his bed.
verses.en_bbe: A door is turned on its pillar, and the hater of work on his bed.

verses.en: The slothful hideth his hand in his bosom; it grieveth him to bring it again to his mouth.
verses.pt: O preguiçoso esconde a sua mão no prato, e nem ao menos quer levá-la de novo à boca.
verses.en_web: The sluggard buries his hand in the dish. He is too lazy to bring it back to his mouth.
verses.en_bbe: The hater of work puts his hand deep into the basin: lifting it again to his mouth is a weariness to him.

verses.en: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit than seven men that can render a reason.
verses.pt: Mais sábio é o preguiçoso a seus olhos do que sete homens que sabem responder bem.
verses.en_web: The sluggard is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who answer with discretion.
verses.en_bbe: The hater of work seems to himself wiser than seven men who are able to give an answer with good sense.

verses.en: He that passeth by, and meddleth with strife belonging not to him, is like one that taketh a dog by the ears.
verses.pt: O que, passando, se mete em questão alheia é como aquele que toma um cão pelas orelhas.
verses.en_web: Like one who grabs a dog’s ears is one who passes by and meddles in a quarrel not his own.
verses.en_bbe: He who gets mixed up in a fight which is not his business, is like one who takes a dog by the ears while it is going by.

verses.en: As a mad man who casteth firebrands, arrows, and death,
verses.pt: Como o louco que atira tições, flechas, e morte,
verses.en_web: Like a madman who shoots torches, arrows, and death,
verses.en_bbe: As one who is off his head sends about flaming sticks and arrows of death,

verses.en: So is the man that deceiveth his neighbour, and saith, Am not I in sport?
verses.pt: assim é o homem que engana o seu próximo, e diz: Fiz isso por brincadeira.
verses.en_web: is the man who deceives his neighbor and says, “Am I not joking?”
verses.en_bbe: So is the man who gets the better of his neighbour by deceit, and says, Am I not doing so in sport?

verses.en: Where no wood is, there the fire goeth out: so where there is no talebearer, the strife ceaseth.
verses.pt: Faltando lenha, apaga-se o fogo; e não havendo difamador, cessa a contenda.
verses.en_web: For lack of wood a fire goes out. Without gossip, a quarrel dies down.
verses.en_bbe: Without wood, the fire goes out; and where there is no secret talk, argument is ended.

verses.en: As coals are to burning coals, and wood to fire; so is a contentious man to kindle strife.
verses.pt: Como o carvão para as brasas, e a lenha para o fogo, assim é o homem contencioso para acender rixas.
verses.en_web: As coals are to hot embers, and wood to fire, so is a contentious man to kindling strife.
verses.en_bbe: Like breath on coals and wood on fire, so a man given to argument gets a fight started.

verses.en: The words of a talebearer are as wounds, and they go down into the innermost parts of the belly.
verses.pt: As palavras do difamador são como bocados deliciosos, que descem ao íntimo do ventre.
verses.en_web: The words of a whisperer are as dainty morsels, they go down into the innermost parts.
verses.en_bbe: The words of one who says evil of his neighbour secretly are like sweet food, they go down into the inner parts of the stomach.

verses.en: Burning lips and a wicked heart are like a potsherd covered with silver dross.
verses.pt: Como o vaso de barro coberto de escória de prata, assim são os lábios ardentes e o coração maligno.
verses.en_web: Like silver dross on an earthen vessel are the lips of a fervent one with an evil heart.
verses.en_bbe: Smooth lips and an evil heart are like a vessel of earth plated with silver waste.

verses.en: He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;
verses.pt: Aquele que odeia dissimula com os seus lábios; mas no seu interior entesoura o engano.
verses.en_web: A malicious man disguises himself with his lips, but he harbors evil in his heart.
verses.en_bbe: With his lips the hater makes things seem what they are not, but deceit is stored up inside him;

verses.en: When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.
verses.pt: Quando te suplicar com voz suave, não o creias; porque sete abominações há no teu coração.
verses.en_web: When his speech is charming, don’t believe him; for there are seven abominations in his heart.
verses.en_bbe: When he says fair words, have no belief in him; for in his heart are seven evils:

verses.en: Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.
verses.pt: Ainda que o seu ódio se encubra com dissimulação, na congregação será revelada a sua malícia.
verses.en_web: His malice may be concealed by deception, but his wickedness will be exposed in the assembly.
verses.en_bbe: Though his hate is covered with deceit, his sin will be seen openly before the meeting of the people.

verses.en: Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein: and he that rolleth a stone, it will return upon him.
verses.pt: O que faz uma cova cairá nela; e a pedra voltará sobre aquele que a revolve.
verses.en_web: Whoever digs a pit shall fall into it. Whoever rolls a stone, it will come back on him.
verses.en_bbe: He who makes a hole in the earth will himself go falling into it: and on him by whom a stone is rolled the stone will come back again.

verses.en: A lying tongue hateth those that are afflicted by it; and a flattering mouth worketh ruin.
verses.pt: A língua falsa odeia aqueles a quem ela tenha ferido; e a boca lisonjeira opera a ruína.
verses.en_web: A lying tongue hates those it hurts; and a flattering mouth works ruin.
verses.en_bbe: A false tongue has hate for those who have clean hearts, and a smooth mouth is a cause of falling.
